title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
statement:
Build a **trie** (prefix tree) that stores lowercase words and answers prefix questions quickly.

Implement `Trie`:
- `Trie()` creates an empty trie.
- `void insert(String word)` adds `word`. Inserting a word twice changes nothing.
- `boolean search(String word)` returns `true` only if `word` itself was inserted. Being a prefix of an inserted word is not enough.
- `boolean startsWith(String prefix)` returns `true` if some inserted word begins with `prefix` (a word counts as a prefix of itself).

Each call should take time proportional to the length of its argument, no matter how many words are stored.

The tests replay a list of operations: `ops[i]` is the method name and `args[i]` its arguments. The expected output has `null` for the constructor and for each `insert`.

examples.output: [null, null, false, true, true, null, true]

constraints: words and prefixes contain only lowercase English letters

target.note: O(L) per operation for a word of length L; words in the benchmark are at most 8 letters, so n operations take O(n)

hints: A HashSet answers search in O(L), but startsWith would have to look at every stored word. What structure lets words that share a beginning share the work of storing it?

Store one node per prefix. Each node has up to 26 children, one per next letter, and a flag that says whether a whole word ends there. search and startsWith both walk down from the root one letter at a time.

Give a private static nested Node class a Node[26] array and a boolean. insert walks the word, creating missing children, then sets the flag on the last node. Write one helper that walks a string and returns the node it lands on, or null if it falls off. search checks that node's flag; startsWith only checks it isn't null.
followups: Node[26] vs HashMap<Character, Node> for the children: what are the memory and speed trade-offs, and when would you switch?
Add a method that returns every stored word starting with a prefix, sorted. What's its complexity?
How would you support search with a '.' wildcard that matches any single letter?
explain: Each trie node represents one prefix: a Node[26] array of children plus a boolean marking that a complete word ends there. insert follows the letters from the root, creating missing nodes, and marks the final one. A shared walk helper returns the node for a string, or null if a child is missing. search needs that node to exist and be marked, so a prefix of a stored word returns false. startsWith only needs it to exist. Every operation is O(L) for an argument of length L, independent of how many words are stored; space is O(total characters inserted × 26) references in the worst case. In Java, compute the child index with word.charAt(i) - 'a', and keep Node a private static nested class so it doesn't hold a hidden reference to the outer object.
